I am 65 years old and I have worked this 6 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I never went to school, but the land has been my teacher. I live alone, so I must plan everything with my own strength in mind—no hired labor, just me and my tools. My well has never run dry, and that is my greatest advantage.

Here is what I will do this year. In early October, I will prepare the field for winter wheat with rotary tillage. This is what nearly everyone in our village does, and it works well on my soil. I will sow an improved wheat variety—probably Jimai or Luyuan502—at about 12.5 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer as a base dose and then topdress with urea twice: once when the wheat greens up in spring, and again at jointing. That gives me about 16 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu in total. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the wheat establish, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. I will spray herbicide once in early spring and apply one more pesticide spray if I see aphids or rust. I expect about 550 kg per mu of wheat if the spring is kind.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize—Denghai605 is what most of us use here—using no-tillage seeding straight into the wheat stubble. There is no time to waste between crops, and at my age I cannot manage deep tillage twice a year. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress with urea at the big trumpet stage, giving about 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. The summer rains usually help, but I will irrigate the maize twice: once if it is dry at sowing, and once at the filling stage. One herbicide application for the maize should be enough. I expect about 600 kg per mu of maize.

This plan is the same one that has fed me for decades. I keep it simple, use my well water wisely, and do not try anything fancy.

I rely on my well for irrigation, giving wheat three critical waterings and maize two. I use improved wheat seeds and hybrid maize seeds with moderate fertilizer rates—compound base plus urea topdressing—and keep pesticides to the minimum needed.
